newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish parliament begins corruption debate.
newsitem.headline: Turkish parliament begins corruption debate.

text.p: Turkish MPs began a parliamentary session on Tuesday to decide whether to send Tansu Ciller, the deputy prime minister, to the Supreme Court on two corruption charges dating from her three-year spell as premier.
Deputies debated a corruption motion against former energy minister Sinasi Altiner ahead of taking up accusations against Ciller.
Two votes were expected later in the day on allegations Ciller abused her power to influence the sale of state-owned carmaker TOFAS and failed to prevent corruption at the TEDAS electricity company.
The Islamist-government would be in deep trouble if coalition partner Ciller lost the votes but analysts predicted a narrow victory.
The opposition is six short of the 276 deputies needed to impeach Ciller and must rely on defections from her True Path Party or Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party.
One True Path deputy resigned just hours before the votes were due but it was unclear why he quit.
Conservative Ciller became Turkey's first woman leader in 1993 but ceded the premiership to Erbakan last year after losing general elections to Welfare in 1995.
She faces a further corruption vote, on the source of her substantial personal wealth, in parliament on Wednesday. The government must also deal with an opposition censure motion next week.
